verses.text: Family, remember this: all our ancestors were under the cloud, and they all crossed through the sea.
They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
They all ate the same spiritual food,
and they all drank the same spiritual drink. They drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and that rock was Christ.
Still, God wasn’t pleased with most of them. Their bodies were scattered across the wilderness.
Those events are warnings for us: don’t crave evil things like they did.
Don’t become idol worshipers like some of them. Scripture says, “The people sat down to eat and drink, then got up to celebrate wildly.”
Let’s not fall into sexual immorality like some of them did—twenty-three thousand died in one day.
Let’s not test Christ like some of them did; they were killed by snakes.
Don’t grumble like some of them did; the destroyer took them out.
These things happened as examples and were written down to warn us, the people living at the turning point of the ages.
So if you think you’re standing strong, watch your step—you could fall.

The temptations you face are the same kind people everywhere face. God is faithful: he won’t let you be tempted beyond what you can handle. With the temptation, he’ll also make a way through so you can endure it.
So, my dear friends, run from idol worship.
I’m talking to people who can think this through—judge what I’m saying.
When we bless the cup, aren’t we sharing in Christ’s blood? When we break the bread, aren’t we sharing in Christ’s body?
Because there’s one loaf, we who are many are one body—we all share that one loaf.
Think about Israel’s people: don’t those who eat the sacrifices share in what’s offered at the altar?
So what am I saying? That food offered to idols is something, or that an idol is real?
No. I’m saying what Gentiles sacrifice, they offer to demons, not to God. I don’t want you sharing life with demons.
You can’t drink the Lord’s cup and demons’ cup too. You can’t share the Lord’s table and the demons’ table.
Are we trying to make the Lord jealous? Are we stronger than he is?
“I’m free to do anything,” but not everything helps. “I’m free to do anything,” but not everything builds people up.
Don’t chase your own good first. Look out for your neighbor’s good.
Eat whatever meat is sold in the market. Don’t interrogate people about it for conscience’s sake,
because “the earth belongs to the Lord, with everything in it.”
If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat whatever’s served. Don’t start questioning it for conscience’s sake.
But if someone says, “This was offered to an idol,” don’t eat it—for the sake of the person who told you and their conscience.
I mean their conscience, not yours. Why should somebody else’s conscience get to judge my freedom?
If I eat with gratitude, why should I get criticized for food I thanked God for?
So whether you eat, drink, or do anything else, do it all for God’s glory.
Don’t trip anybody up—Jews, Greeks, or God’s church.
That’s what I try to do: please everyone in every way, not chasing my own benefit but looking out for many, so they can be saved.
